hypothesis_or_artifact: Section 14 B.3 replay schedule (the registered reopen path for Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, GLM-5.2) and the power floor the code enforces
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: Each model replays when the calendar grows its clean window past the registered power floor, detectable IC 0.025 at 30 names, which needs roughly 221 trading days after its own guard band.
evidence_summary: The 221-day trigger is 2.0*0.185695/sqrt(221)=0.0250, i.e. the null sd with no overlap adjustment (definition at REGISTRATION.md:208-212; code registered_floor_mde at src/npd/power.py:129-131). The closure re-sizes the design on realized dispersion to 'near 1,700 trading days' (REGISTRATION.md:716-718) but leaves Section 14 unamended, so the registered reopen trigger and the closure's own sizing differ by a factor of about eight. On the realized model daily-IC sd of 0.25159 (n 404) the same 0.025 floor needs (2*0.25159/0.025)^2 = 405 days with no overlap adjustment and about 1,377 at the registered VIF 3.4; on the realized coin-test bootstrap half-width of 0.0337 at 404 days (evaluation.md:133, :250-251) the replay window would need about 734 days. Hygiene folded in: the registration carries two different floors. Section 3's window table registers a day-count minimum, '| registered minimum | 200 |' (REGISTRATION.md:84), and the code implements exactly that -- clears_power_floor=len(inside) >= cfg.min_trading_days (src/npd/window.py:76) with min_trading_days=200 (src/npd/config.py:80), Section 0 firing BLOCKED on the count (src/npd/section0.py:56-61). Section 9.1's IC-0.025 power floor implies 221 days (REGISTRATION.md:208-212, :377-379), and 200 days gives 2.0*0.185695/sqrt(200)=0.02626 > 0.025, so the two registered floors disagree with each other and a window clearing the 200-day minimum need not clear the power floor the B.3 schedule names; the code is faithful to the first floor. The closure names no revised replay date and the post-anchor marker _CLOSED_DO_NOT_RUN_HERE (untracked, dated 2026-09-02, read 2026-09-03T06:30:46Z, UNANCHORED) directs successor work to a new repository, so the registered reopen path has neither a valid trigger nor an owner.
recomputation: Inputs: null sd 0.185695 (REGISTRATION.md:203-204), t 2.0 (config.py:119), VIF 3.4 (REGISTRATION.md:225), realized model IC sd 0.25159 (n 404), realized coin half-width 0.0337 (evaluation.md:250-251). Method: days = (t*sd/MDE)^2 * VIF. Results: 220.7 days (registered inputs), 750 (registered sd at VIF 3.4), 405 (realized sd, no overlap), 1,377 (realized sd at VIF 3.4), ~734 (coin half-width route); and MDE 0.02626 at the 200-day minimum registered at REGISTRATION.md:84 and implemented in config.py:80. Script scratchpad/work/agentA/recompute.py.

hypothesis_or_artifact: The low-reasoning-effort variant named in Amendment 2 as a future registered variant, versus the Closure's 'What a powered version would cost'
label: READ
claim_quote:
Sizing against the measured 0.36339 rather than the registered assumption requires roughly **four times the evaluable days**, landing near **1,700 trading days** of post-cutoff window.

**No model has one.** The window would have to accumulate from the calendar at about 21 trading days a month.
evidence_summary: The closure prices exactly one route to a powered result, calendar accumulation to about 1,700 days, and declares it unavailable. It does not mention the variant the registration itself named seven amendments earlier (REGISTRATION.md:493-496), nor the 3.0622 USD left under the cap (REGISTRATION.md:789-790), nor what that variant would cost now that Amendment 4's strict schema is in force. A price for it does exist in the registration, in Amendment 2's calibration table -- low at 0.027271 USD per call and 11.7812 USD projected over 432 days (REGISTRATION.md:471-474), repeated at 'low projects 11.7812 USD and fails it' (REGISTRATION.md:476-477) -- but it is stale: the ledger's realized rate is 0.03735 USD per call against the calibrated 0.027271 and 3,110 reasoning tokens against 2,432, so the same 432-day run now prices near 16.13 USD, about 37 percent above the projection, and the closure's cost section carries neither figure. Ledger-measured cost of the 70 low attempts under the in-force digest (live ledgers/evidence.jsonl, read 2026-09-03T06:35:37Z, UNANCHORED): mean 0.03735 USD per attempt, mean 3,110 reasoning tokens, 53 of 70 attempts stored (76 percent), mean latency 31.5 s. A full 432-day low collection projects to about 16.1 USD at one attempt per day and about 21.3 USD at the realized 1.32 attempts per stored low day; the 365-day window Amendment 2 named as the road not taken (REGISTRATION.md:488-490, which sizes the window and its MDE 0.0194 and carries no USD figure) prices on the same ledger rates at about 13.6 to 18.0 USD, which is this audit's arithmetic and not the registration's. The binding blocker is the leftover balance, not the calendar (REGISTRATION.md:293-295). Every sentence of the closure carries the effort qualifier (session_a1_b1.md:261-263; REGISTRATION.md:483-486), and the only in-sample datum on that qualifier, the split of AUDIT-A-NPDExperiment-2, reads +0.0509 on 51 low days against -0.0004 on 353 minimal days at the primary horizon: imprecise but on the hypothesis side. Honest limit: the low variant would not repair the contrast power at 432 days (the contrast-sd problem of AUDIT-A-NPDExperiment-1 is independent of effort), so its value is confined to the effort qualifier: the omission is of the price of the route to the qualifier every closure sentence carries, not of an alternative route to a powered contrast, and 'No model has one' is correctly scoped to the 1,700-day window.

Method: mean over low attempts with the in-force digest; multiply by 432 and by 432 x 70/53. Result: 16.13 USD at one attempt per day, 21.3 USD at the realized 1.32 attempts per stored low day; 365-day version 13.6 to 18.0 USD. Script scratchpad/work/agentA/supp.py, output supp.out.
would_resolve: Add to the closure's cost section the price of the named low variant (order 15 to 25 USD on the ledger's own rates, against Amendment 2's now-stale 11.7812 USD) beside the 1,700-day route, recorded explicitly as the route to the effort qualifier every closure sentence carries rather than as an alternative route to a powered contrast, and state whether it is declined on cost, on the operator decision recorded at REGISTRATION.md:710, or on the contrast-power argument. The closure's 'No model has one' is correctly scoped to the 1,700-day window; with the variant's price beside it, it stops reading as 'no achievable path exists' for the qualifier as well.
confidence_why: The omission and the measured cost are firm, but whether the variant is worth running is a judgement the closure is entitled to make and simply did not make.
invalidation_note: No commits after the anchor; the untracked 2026-09-02 marker says successor work belongs in a new repository, which is consistent with the variant still being open.
disclosure_ref: NPDExperiment/REGISTRATION.md:493-496 names the low-effort shortened-window variant as a natural candidate for a future registered variant, and NPDExperiment/REGISTRATION.md:710 states the closure is by operator decision, not by evidence. What the closure's cost section does not carry is the variant's cost: the registration's own projection of 11.7812 USD over 432 days (REGISTRATION.md:471-474, :476-477) sits in Amendment 2, pre-dates Amendment 4's strict schema, and is stale by about 37 percent against the ledger-measured 16.13 USD (0.03735 against 0.027271 USD per call; 3,110 against 2,432 reasoning tokens).
